chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man killed a man in the Sanctuary.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a wergild and a third, and he must fast two consecutive months from the Sacred Months, and emancipate a neck, and feed sixty poor people.'
I said: 'Does something enter into this?' He said: 'And what would it be?' I said: 'The two Eids, and the days of Tashreeq?' He said: 'He must fast them, for it is a right necessitated upon him.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing someone in the Sanctuary according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the comprehensive expiation (kaffarah) for homicide within the Sanctuary, emphasizing the cumulative nature of penalties including blood money, manumission, feeding the poor, and fasting. A key scholarly nuance highlighted here is the Imam’s clarification that the fasting obligation is absolute and not suspended during Eid al-Adha or the Days of Tashreeq, distinguishing it from other voluntary or specific fasts. This ruling underscores the severity of the crime and the rigor of the penance required to satisfy divine justice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Bin taghlub, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man kills a man in the Sanctuary’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a wergild and a third, and he would Fast two months consecutively from the Sacred months, and he would emancipate (liberate) a neck, and he would feed sixty poor ones’.

I said, ‘(Supposing) something enters into this?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what would it be?’ I said, ‘The two Eids, and the days of Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup>, & 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would Fast it, for it is a right necessitated upon him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Aban ibn Taghlib from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who kills a man in the sacred area. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one full and a half blood money, wergild. He fasts for two consecutive months of the sacred months, sets free a slave and feeds sixty destitute people.’

I then said, ‘What happens if something comes in between?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Give an example.’ I said, ‘The two ‘Id and the days of tashriq (11, 12, and 13).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to fast because it is an established right on him.’”
